transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-17 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 min
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Cardinal - Head of MLOps), Tom Reeves (Cardinal - VP Product), Ellen Park (Cardinal - Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): Focus on prioritizing health signals and agreeing pilot scope; discuss cost/latency tradeoffs and security checklist.

[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, appreciate it. Quick roll call — Maria here, Devon's with me.
[00:06] Tom Reeves: Tom here — sorry running a bit late, got pulled into a quick stand.
[00:10] Priya Singh: Priya, good to be here.
[00:12] Ellen Park: Ellen here.
[00:14] Maria Chen: Great. The plan for today: high-level health signals we've seen, go over cost/usage trends, then talk pilot scope — six weeks we discussed — and close with next steps and security items. If we run over Devon will do a short deep-dive on the benchmark run-book.
[00:30] Devon Patel: Hi all, I'll try to keep the perf stuff practical.
[00:35] Priya Singh: Cool. To start, we've been seeing a 40% month-over-month rise on inference calls since December, most of it from our recommendations flow. Latency spikes at peak are pushing 800 to 1,000 ms p95 on our current infra, and cost per 1k tokens is trending up about 22% month-over-month.
[00:55] Maria Chen: Okay that's helpful. Do you know how much of that is long-context versus short prompts?
[01:00] Priya Singh: Mostly short prompts 30-60 tokens; we have a smaller percentage of long conversation with KV cache usage but it's not the driver. Strange thing is the p95 is spiky even for short prompts.
[01:15] Devon Patel: That usually signals resource contention on the serving side — small requests get queued behind heavier seq-lens, or autoscale thresholds are misaligned. On Redwood we see options: smarter batching, prefix/KV caching and also dedicated pools for predictable tail latency.
[01:30] Tom Reeves: We're trying to avoid dedicated GPUs unless we absolutely need them, budget is tight. Can you give an apples-to-apples on cost delta hosted vs dedicated?
[01:45] Maria Chen: Sure — ballpark: for steady throughput with tight p95 SLOs, Dedicated can drop tail latency variance by ~40-60% and unit cost is lower at scale because of reserved capacity, but you trade commit and minimum monthly spend. Hosted is great for bursty traffic and no-ops. We'll share a pricing sheet that models Cardinal's sample traffic.
[02:05] Priya Singh: The commit is the harder sell to finance. They'd prefer pilot first.
[02:10] Maria Chen: Agreed, pilot is the right next step. For pilot success criteria, what would you prioritize? Latency p95 under 300 ms, overall cost no more than the current spend + 10%, and model output parity?
[02:25] Tom Reeves: That sounds reasonable. Also need logs and audit for compliance — we just started SOC2 scoping.
[02:33] Ellen Park: Yes on SOC2, and we need KMS integration for customer-sensitive tokens. We use a cloud KMS (Azure) and also want RBAC for key routes.
[02:45] Devon Patel: We support KMS integrations and a VPC/private deployment for pilot if you want — there's a small setup window — or we can do hosted with envelope encryption and a customer-managed key. There's an option for Private (VPC) where the control plane stays in Redwood but the inference nodes are in your VPC.
[03:05] Priya Singh: How long does the VPC setup usually take? We're not air-gapped but network approvals can take two weeks.
[03:12] Maria Chen: The VPC onboarding is typically 7–14 business days depending on your cloud security team. For the pilot we could start hosted (fast) then flip to VPC for the second phase.
[03:22] Tom Reeves: That split approach could work — start with hosted benchmarks, then move to private if performance/controls justify it.
[03:30] Devon Patel: For the benchmarks I propose a two-step run: 1) Functional parity: run your top 20 prompts with current model and our recommended model/quantization, capture outputs and basic evals; 2) Load and tail-latency: replay traffic samples at peak QPS with realistic sequence lengths, measuring p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
[03:52] Priya Singh: What's the quantization story? We saw a note about 4-bit quant that cut token cost in a different vendor demo but worried about hallucinations.
[04:00] Devon Patel: Yeah, quantization reduces memory and can lower per-token CPU time, but you need to validate output quality. For many workloads 4-bit QAT or advanced post-train quant works well, but we will include side-by-side evals. The Redwood Optimize tooling suggests quantization profiles per model/latency target.
[04:18] Ellen Park: Do you have an example of the unit economics per million tokens for the quantized vs non-quantized path?
[04:25] Maria Chen: We'll include that in the pricing sheet — we'll prototype two scenarios in the pilot: default FP16 (or int8 where available) and int4/int4+ quantized variant with quality thresholds.
[04:36] Tom Reeves: On reliability, we've had a few incidents where a partial region outage caused fallbacks to an older model that wasn't compatible and the app crashed. Can Redwood do automatic variant fallbacks?
[04:48] Devon Patel: Yes — smart routing allows fallbacks to compatible model variants. You can set a policy to fallback regionally or to a lower-cost variant when exact variant isn't available. We'll also add a canary policy during rollouts.
[05:00] Priya Singh: Good — we need automatic, but also transparency. We want to know when fallback happened and why.
[05:06] Maria Chen: The console has route-level tracing and audit logs for rollouts and fallbacks, and we can stream notifications to your pager.
[05:14] Ellen Park: What's stored in audit logs? Are prompts part of logs or redacted by default?
[05:20] Devon Patel: Prompts are sensitive; by default we redact PII and you can choose retention and redaction level. For enterprise private deployments, customers can control retention fully. We'll attach the security matrix.
[05:32] Tom Reeves: Okay. Let's talk pilot scope: you said six weeks — can we make it 4 weeks for the functional + 2 weeks for load?
[05:40] Maria Chen: That's what we typically do: 2 weeks integration/functional, 2 weeks perf tuning + quant eval, and 2 weeks production-like load and SLA verification. If Cardinal wants to compress, we can do 4-week condensed but risk less tuning time.
[05:55] Priya Singh: Finance would push for the shorter timeline. Do we lose anything critical if compressed?
[05:59] Devon Patel: Tuning batch/serve settings and route policies benefits from incremental iterations; compressing reduces ability to catch intermittent tail issues. If you do condensed, we'll prioritize p95 tail testing and a stop-gap set of cache/batching configs.
[06:14] Ellen Park: For the trial data, what's the best way to share sample traffic? We can't share PII.
[06:20] Maria Chen: A scrubbing script works; many customers send an anonymized sample with entity placeholders. We'll provide a template and an S3 presigned link for upload.
[06:29] Tom Reeves: On cost again — can Redwood provide an estimate of monthly savings if we move to a reserved dedicated pool at our projected QPS?
[06:36] Maria Chen: Yes — we'll model that in the pricing sheet. You mentioned 40% month-over-month growth; if that trajectory holds, committed Dedicated typically shows savings after a 3-month break-even on consistent traffic. We'll show a break-even graph.
[06:50] Priya Singh: Great. Security nuance: we need to surface SOC2 type II evidence and pen test cadence.
[06:56] Devon Patel: Redwood has SOC2 Type II reports and an annual pen test. We'll share the compliance pack, including audit log retention options and our SOC2 scope.
[07:05] Tom Reeves: Any customer references in regulated verticals?
[07:09] Maria Chen: We can share a couple—one in fintech that went through SOC2 and market compliance; we'll get consent and redact as needed.
[07:17] Priya Singh: Back to signals — we want to prioritize instrumentation. Right now we have three signal buckets: latency (p95/p99), token cost, and output quality drift. Which should come first?
[07:30] Devon Patel: I'd recommend latency p95 + output quality drift as the top two. You can automate alerts on p95 and set a quality regression threshold on a small evaluation set. Token cost is important but is often managed post-stability through quant and batching.
[07:45] Maria Chen: For tooling: Redwood Optimize can generate batching and cache suggestions and tie changes to eval sets so you can see quality/cost impact.
[07:55] Ellen Park: We want a dashboard with token spend breakdown by route and model. Is that available?
[07:59] Devon Patel: Yep — console shows token-level breakdown per route, per model, and also per token type (input vs generated) for cost attribution.
[08:08] Tom Reeves: Ok, logistics — what do we need from us to get pilot started?
[08:12] Maria Chen: Three things: 1) sample traffic + top 20 prompts; 2) confirmation of compliance constraints (KMS choice, retention max); 3) a list of stakeholders and uptime SLO target.
[08:24] Priya Singh: We can pull sample traffic and prompts by Thursday, and agree SLOs internally.
[08:28] Tom Reeves: Finance will need the pilot cost number — not just committed pricing.
[08:32] Maria Chen: We'll provide a pilot cost estimate in the SOW — that's non-binding but close.
[08:36] Devon Patel: Quick note on benchmarking: we'll run two model variants: a lower-latency tuned model and a quality-first model, both with quant profiles. We'll show per-token cost and p95/p99.
[08:50] Priya Singh: If the quantized model shows a 2% drop in accuracy on NP tasks, do you support fallback to the higher-precision model automatically?
[08:58] Devon Patel: Yes — we can implement a route-level policy: if quality metric dips below threshold, switch traffic to the other variant and notify you.
[09:06] Ellen Park: One more — can we get rate-limit testing and burst behavior documented? Our app sometimes has 2–3x bursts for a few seconds.
[09:14] Maria Chen: We'll include burst tests in the load suite and show autoscale behavior and cold-start risk.
[09:20] Tom Reeves: Anything else from you guys?
[09:22] Priya Singh: Quick ask — show the console view of trace that shows fallback events, not just logs.
[09:28] Maria Chen: We'll do a live short demo of that in the kick-off deep dive.
[09:32] Devon Patel: For the SOW we'll include milestone checkpoints: integration complete, functional verification, perf run, post-run review.
[09:40] Tom Reeves: Sounds good, what are the dates again for deliverables?
[09:43] Maria Chen: We'll share SOW by 2027-02-22, you upload traffic by 2027-02-24, Devon will deliver benchmark harness by 2027-02-25, and then target kick-off week of 2027-02-28.
[10:00] Priya Singh: That timeline works for us.
[10:03] Ellen Park: I'll schedule internal infra approvals for the VPC if needed.
[10:07] Maria Chen: Quick recap — pilot scope: 6-week pilot with staged approach (hosted start, optional VPC). Success criteria: p95 under 300 ms, cost within +10% of current, quality parity on top 20 prompts. Deliverables: SOW + pricing, benchmark harness, sample upload instructions, security pack. Next steps as we listed.
[10:30] Tom Reeves: Thanks all.
[10:33] Priya Singh: Thanks.
[10:35] Maria Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the SOW and calendar invites.
